::: {#exm-equivariance}

#### ReLU and max pooling

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
relu, pool = nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2)
with torch.no_grad():
    maps = conv(x_test[:1])
    relu_gap = (relu(shift_right(maps)) - shift_right(relu(maps))).abs().max().item()
    pooled_shift = pool(shift_right(maps))
    pooled = pool(maps)
pool_shape = list(pooled.shape[2:])
pool_gap = (pooled_shift - pooled).abs().max().item()
print(relu_gap, pool_shape, pool_gap)
```

A [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu) acts on each pixel separately.
So it is [translation equivariant](#def-equivariance) with no edge effect.
On the [feature maps](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-feature-map) of `conv` for a test digit,
`relu(shift_right(maps))` and `shift_right(relu(maps))` `r if (py$relu_gap == 0) "agree exactly" else sprintf("differ by at most %.1e", py$relu_gap)`.
A $2 \times 2$ max [pooling](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-pooling) layer is not translation equivariant.
Its output is `r py$pool_shape[[1]]` by `r py$pool_shape[[2]]`.
A shift of one input pixel is half an output pixel.
No shift of the output can match it.
The pooled maps of the shifted and unshifted input differ by up to `r sprintf("%.2f", py$pool_gap)`.

:::
